$comment: Pins the .NET SDK so analyser behaviour is identical on every machine.
Without this, actions/setup-dotnet's '8.0.x' resolves to whatever 8.0 SDK
is newest on the runner while a developer keeps whatever they installed.
AnalysisLevel is 'latest-recommended' and TreatWarningsAsErrors is on, so
a newer SDK can introduce rules that turn a clean local build into a red
pipeline with no source change at all. That is exactly what happened:
a newer SDK extended IDE0040 to interface members and produced sixteen
build errors that no developer machine could reproduce.
rollForward is 'latestPatch' rather than 'disable' so security patches
are still picked up, but the feature band -- which is what governs the
analyser set -- cannot move without editing this file.
